title: November 2026: the GUI shootout, again
model: Claude Opus 5.5 (high effort), one agent per toolkit, in OpenCode

toolkits.name: WebUI (reference)
toolkits.summary: The reference app every toolkit was compared against, shown in Chromium with the first-launch setup dialog.

shots.caption: The reference WebUI at 1280×800 with the first-launch setup dialog

toolkits.name: Flutter
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Near pixel match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Close to pixel-level with the reference, with every page, data source, action and setup step working.
toolkits.lessons: Fonts were the main fight: the Linux engine ignores fontconfig aliases, so the agent loads Chromium's faces itself. dart:io cannot create process groups, so cancel uses setsid plus a watchdog.

linux.build: ~25 s clean release build once the SDK is warm

windows.notes: Warm median of 5; 4.8 s first launch after VM boot; ~0.9 s is engine start on a GPU-less VM.

toolkits.name: Compose Desktop
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Near pixel match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Every control is hand-made from Compose foundation primitives styled after the reference CSS, so the window is close to pixel-for-pixel.
toolkits.lessons: Material looks nothing like the reference and AWT cannot pick folders on Linux, so controls are custom and the picker shells out to zenity. The JVM tax shows in startup, memory and a 187 MB distributable.

linux.build: ~31 s clean with dependencies cached; jlink JRE + AppCDS
linux.note: Measured at load average ~7.4; 862–935 ms at normal load.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: wxPython
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match; native GTK controls under the hood.
toolkits.summary: Native GTK entries, choices and file choosers sit inside custom-drawn chrome, very close to the reference.
toolkits.lessons: There are no Linux wxPython wheels, so it runs from a ~1 GB conda-forge environment, and a GLX probing hang under a fresh Xvfb needed a bundled Mesa. wx itself was the easy part.

linux.build: ~11 min cold (pixi install of wxPython, GTK and Mesa); 0.3 s warm
linux.note: Size is the app-local conda-forge environment, mostly GTK and Mesa.

toolkits.name: Qt 6 / QML
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Main shot matches the reference closely.
toolkits.summary: A C++ backend with a compiled-in QML front end; the full workflow works and the screenshots are almost identical to the reference.
toolkits.lessons: Qt Quick fit the app well. CSS grid sizing, native select popups and Chromium's font fallbacks had to be approximated, and without a SIGTERM handler killed apps orphaned their child processes.

linux.build: 84 s clean (cmake + make, -j2)
linux.note: Single binary; needs the system Qt 6 runtime.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog
A command streaming output, with Cancel

toolkits.name: GTK4 / libadwaita (Rust)
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Faithful layout, but the setup dialog is libadwaita-styled (centred text, blue button) rather than the reference look.
toolkits.summary: Native GTK 4 and libadwaita covering the whole workflow, close to the reference with deliberate native touches such as Adwaita dialogs and header-bar controls.
toolkits.lessons: Rebuilding the page on every change loses focus, so widgets get stable names to restore it, and Rc/RefCell re-entrancy needs care. Without a window manager, RTL windows land off-screen.

linux.build: 2 min 10 s clean release (-j2, thin LTO)

toolkits.name: Slint
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Every page renders through custom Slint components tuned against the reference CSS; the main window is very close to the reference.
toolkits.lessons: Slint cannot create widgets at runtime, so every control shape is declared up front and chosen by kind. Bindings break once the user types, and there is no RTL layout direction.

linux.build: ~5 min clean release (-j4); 70–130 s incremental

toolkits.name: Avalonia
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Plain C# with no XAML, rebuilt from the bundle on each change, shipped as a 22 MB NativeAOT binary that is ready in about 0.2 s.
toolkits.lessons: No hard blockers: building the UI in code worked well. The real library table and genome dropdowns could only be checked in their error state, without the installed CLI runtime.

linux.build: 59 s clean NativeAOT publish (2 cores)
linux.note: No .NET runtime needed at run time.

windows.notes: Warm median of 5; 1349 ms first launch after VM boot. NativeAOT.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: PySide6 (Qt Widgets)
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Qt Widgets in Python with a stylesheet generated from the reference's CSS variables; it differs mainly in font rendering and scrollbars.
toolkits.lessons: No blockers, since the wheels bundle Qt. Qt has no CSS grid or flex-wrap, so it needed a custom flow layout, and controls update in place because re-rendering loses focus.

linux.build: 0.4 s (uv sync; nothing compiled)
linux.note: Size excludes the 115 MB uv-managed CPython.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: egui
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Every widget is hand-painted in immediate mode, so the screenshots line up with the reference almost pixel for pixel.
toolkits.lessons: API churn in egui 0.37 made existing examples stale. egui has no bidi, so RTL needed hand-written reordering, and the custom widgets lack accessibility.

linux.build: ~4 min clean release (-j4); 12–15 s incremental

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: Iced
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Elm-style Iced on the tiny-skia CPU renderer, matching the reference almost pixel for pixel with the lowest memory use so far.
toolkits.lessons: Two tiny-skia renderer bugs (text escaping scroll clipping, blurred shadows erasing what is under them) cost the most time. Iced has no layout direction, so RTL is mirrored by hand.

linux.build: 3 min 36 s clean release (-j4); ~75 s incremental

toolkits.name: Tkinter
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Layout matches, but no dimmed backdrop behind dialogs and flatter controls.
toolkits.summary: Rounded controls come from Pillow-generated 9-slice ttk images, giving a look close to the reference with the smallest memory use so far.
toolkits.lessons: uv's Python ships Tk without Xft (bitmap fonts only), so it runs on conda-forge Tk. Tk 8.6 has no bidi, so Hebrew and Arabic text renders in logical order.

linux.build: 0.6 s (pixi install; nothing compiled)
linux.note: Size is the app-local conda-forge Python, Tk and Pillow.

toolkits.name: GTK4 / libadwaita (Python)
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Faithful layout, libadwaita-styled dialog and title bar diverge from the reference.
toolkits.summary: About 3,900 lines of Python on the system PyGObject, with native Adwaita widgets styled with CSS to match the reference.
toolkits.lessons: The harness's GTK_THEME broke libadwaita, and RTL windows land off-screen without a window manager. Memory is the weak spot: about 250 MB with software GL.

linux.build: 15 s clean; nothing compiled
linux.note: Measured at load average ~10; 707–985 ms on repeat runs.

toolkits.name: Fyne
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Very close to the reference, though Fyne's stock widgets only got part of the way: buttons, tooltips, the modal and most layouts are custom.
toolkits.lessons: Fyne has one fixed look, theme padding everywhere and no flex-wrap. It has no native file dialogs on Linux and no paragraph bidi.

linux.build: 2 min 9 s cold (go build -p 2); 1.4 s incremental

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: Gio
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: Close match to the reference.
toolkits.summary: Very close to the reference down to colours and spacing, though Gio's few stock widgets meant the dropdown, tooltips, table, modal and layouts are all custom.
toolkits.lessons: Layout constraints and linear-space colour blending cost the most time. Gio has no folder picker on Linux, so it shells out to zenity or kdialog.

linux.build: 14 s cold (-p 2); ~2 s incremental
linux.note: RSS is mostly software GL (llvmpipe) and NVIDIA EGL libraries under the harness.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: Toga / BeeWare
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: very close layout; the setup dialog has no shadow and controls are flatter.
toolkits.summary: Toga's GTK 3 backend renders the whole workflow very close to the reference, with one app-wide GTK stylesheet and a few native escape hatches doing the styling.
toolkits.lessons: Toga's Pack layout has no borders, radii, tooltips, label wrapping or checkbox, so text is pre-broken with Pango and switches stand in for checkboxes. Modal dialogs are faked with a second window.

linux.build: 0.65 s (uv venv on system PyGObject; nothing compiled)
linux.note: Size excludes the system Python, PyGObject and GTK 3.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog (private workspace)

toolkits.name: Textual
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: remarkably faithful for a terminal (layout, scrim, dialog, icons), but monospace cell grid, one text size and a pixelated app icon.
toolkits.summary: A terminal UI with the reference's layout, colours and full workflow, shown in a vendored kitty terminal that also draws the real bundle icon.
toolkits.lessons: A TUI is a monospace cell grid, so there is no large title and controls are flat one-row fields. Shipping it as a window means vendoring a terminal, and Textual has no native dialogs or RTL.

linux.build: 2.4 s clean (kitty download + uv sync; nothing compiled)
linux.note: About 237 MB of the RSS and 163 MB of the size are the vendored kitty terminal; the Python app alone is ~60 MB RSS and 33 MB.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog, in kitty

toolkits.name: GPUI
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: nearly identical to the reference, including dialog shadow and focus ring.
toolkits.summary: Zed's GPUI, through gpui-kit and gpui-component, renders the whole workflow within a pixel or two of the reference, including dialog shadows, focus rings, RTL and a dark theme.
toolkits.lessons: Picking a crate is the hard part: the crates.io gpui is old, so it builds on gpui-kit, a recent Zed snapshot whose API shifts between releases. It pulls in ~800 dependencies for a 43 MB binary, and file dialogs work only through xdg-desktop-portal.

linux.build: 9 min 27 s first clean build (-j4, ~600 crates); ~26 s app-only rebuild
linux.note: Ready time measured on a busy machine; 213–225 ms earlier on a quieter one. Built with gpui-kit (a recent Zed snapshot).

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: Makepad
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: nearly identical to the reference. RTL is not mirrored and there is no dark theme.
toolkits.summary: Pages are built at runtime by a custom widget that instantiates Makepad's live-DSL templates from the bundle JSON; the main window is very close to the reference and nearly the whole workflow works.
toolkits.lessons: Makepad's DSL is static, so a dynamic widget tree needed custom code, and two text bugs (word wrap, RTL scripts) had to be fixed in a vendored, patched makepad-draw. There are no native file dialogs, RTL layout or dark theme.

linux.build: 1 min 52 s clean release (-j2); ~10 s incremental
linux.note: About 270 MB of the RSS is a bare Makepad window under software GL (llvmpipe). Size is a 9.2 MB binary, 2.9 MB of resources and ~48 MB of Makepad fonts read from the cargo registry.

shots.caption: First launch with the setup dialog

toolkits.name: Moonframe
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: close layout and dialog; different icon set, slightly larger scale, and a debug line left in the terminal panel.
toolkits.summary: The whole window is Luau mods on Moonframe's GPUI renderer, fed by Rust providers for the bundle, processes and terminal; it matches the reference closely in layout and light theme.
toolkits.lessons: Luau live reload made iteration fast: after a handful of Rust builds, every layout and style change was a Luau edit and a recapture in seconds. GPUI needed a vendored lavapipe to run under Xvfb, and the library owns the command line and the terminal, so both needed workarounds.

linux.build: 18 min clean release (-j2, no lease); ~10 s incremental; Luau changes need no rebuild
linux.note: Ready time measured at load ~7 (~740 ms on a quieter run). Size includes 15 MB of vendored lavapipe, needed only under Xvfb.

toolkits.name: Zenbu UI
toolkits.myNotes: Provisional, from the main screenshot: nearly identical to the reference.
toolkits.summary: A native X11/GL window on Zenbu, a private C immediate-mode UI stack, rendering the whole WGS Extract workflow close to the reference with light and dark themes and right-to-left mirroring.
toolkits.lessons: As a private monorepo with no packaged release, Zenbu had to be built from a mirrored scratch workspace with the app overlaid. Its core is fast and its bidi text just works, but form-level widgets, RTL mirroring and wake-ups on child output were all hand-built, and images draw as black boxes under software GL.

linux.build: 178 s clean optimised build (2 cores, cache warm); ~30 s incremental
linux.note: RSS is mostly Mesa llvmpipe and font arenas.
